events.label: Whitlam ALP
events.description: Gough Whitlam wins federal election, ending 23 years of Coalition government. Introduced Medicare predecessor Medibank, free university education, and the Family Law Act.

events.label: Medibank
events.description: Medibank — Australia's first universal health insurance scheme — launched by the Whitlam government. The precursor to Medicare.

events.label: Fraser LNP
events.description: Malcolm Fraser wins election following the constitutional crisis and dismissal of Whitlam government by Governor-General John Kerr.

events.label: Recession
events.description: Australia's 1982–83 recession. Unemployment peaked at 10.4%. Triggered by global interest rate rises and drought.

events.label: Hawke ALP
events.description: Bob Hawke wins federal election. Begins era of major economic reform including floating the dollar, bank deregulation and the Accord with unions.

events.label: AUD floated
events.description: Hawke-Keating government floats the Australian dollar, deregulating the exchange rate. A landmark economic reform that exposed Australia to global capital markets.

events.label: Banks deregulated
events.description: Foreign banks allowed to operate in Australia. Beginning of financial deregulation that eventually contributed to household debt growth.

events.label: Medicare
events.description: Medicare universal health insurance system launched by the Hawke government, replacing Medibank. Provides free or subsidised access to medical services for all Australians.

events.label: Super introduced
events.description: Compulsory superannuation introduced by Keating government at 3%, rising to 9% then 11.5%. Now manages over $3.5 trillion — the fourth largest pension pool in the world.

events.label: Keating ALP
events.description: Paul Keating defeats Bob Hawke in Labor leadership ballot, becomes PM. Wins the 1993 'unwinnable' election.

events.label: Recession
events.description: The recession 'we had to have' — Keating's description. Unemployment hit 11.2%. Triggered by high interest rates (17.5%) and a credit crunch following financial deregulation.

events.label: Native Title
events.description: Native Title Act passed following the landmark Mabo High Court decision, recognising Indigenous Australians' rights to land for the first time.

events.label: Howard LNP
events.description: John Howard wins federal election, beginning 11-year Coalition government. Introduced gun buyback, GST and Work Choices.

events.label: Gun buyback
events.description: Howard government's National Firearms Agreement and buyback scheme following Port Arthur massacre. Over 650,000 firearms surrendered.

events.label: Asian crisis
events.description: Asian Financial Crisis. Australia largely avoided recession but terms of trade and export revenues were hit. Thailand, Indonesia and South Korea severely affected.

events.label: GST
events.description: Goods and Services Tax (GST) introduced at 10% by Howard government. Replaced wholesale sales tax. Caused temporary CPI spike on introduction.

events.label: Sept 11
events.description: September 11 terrorist attacks in the United States. Triggered global economic slowdown, surge in defence spending and counter-terrorism legislation in Australia.

events.label: Mining boom
events.description: China-driven mining boom transforms Australian economy. Terms of trade hit 140-year high in 2011. Insulated Australia from GFC. Iron ore price rose from $15 to $180 per tonne.

events.label: WorkChoices
events.description: Howard government's WorkChoices industrial relations legislation. Weakened unfair dismissal protections and collective bargaining. Widely credited with costing Howard the 2007 election.

events.label: Rudd ALP
events.description: Kevin Rudd wins federal election. Labor returns after 11 years. Signs Kyoto Protocol on first day in office.

events.label: GFC
events.description: Global Financial Crisis. Australia avoided recession through $42bn stimulus package. RBA cut rates from 7.25% to 3.0% in 7 months. Only major economy to avoid negative growth.

events.label: Gillard ALP
events.description: Julia Gillard replaces Kevin Rudd as PM — Australia's first female Prime Minister. Wins 2010 election with minority government.

events.label: Carbon price
events.description: Carbon pricing mechanism introduced by Gillard government at $23/tonne. Reduced emissions but politically toxic — repealed by Abbott in 2014.

events.label: NDIS launched
events.description: National Disability Insurance Scheme trial launched by Gillard government. Provides individualised funding for Australians with permanent and significant disability. Now supports over 600,000 people and costs ~$42bn per year — the fastest-growing area of government spending.

events.label: Gonski reforms
events.description: Gonski school funding reforms announced — needs-based funding model for Australian schools. Partially implemented by Gillard, contested by subsequent governments.

events.label: Abbott LNP
events.description: Tony Abbott wins federal election with Coalition majority. Repeals carbon tax, cuts foreign aid and begins Operation Sovereign Borders offshore processing.

events.label: Carbon tax repealed
events.description: Abbott government repeals carbon pricing mechanism. Australia becomes the first country to repeal a carbon price. Emissions subsequently rose.

events.label: Mining bust
events.description: End of mining investment boom as China's growth slows. Iron ore falls from $135 to $40/tonne. Terms of trade decline sharply. WA and QLD severely affected.

events.label: Turnbull LNP
events.description: Malcolm Turnbull replaces Tony Abbott as PM in Liberal leadership challenge. Wins 2016 election with one-seat majority.

events.label: Negative gearing debate
events.description: Labor announces policy to limit negative gearing to new properties. Triggers major national debate about housing affordability vs investor returns. Coalition retains negative gearing.

events.label: Banking RC
events.description: Royal Commission into Misconduct in the Banking, Superannuation and Financial Services Industry established. Uncovered widespread misconduct including charging fees to dead customers.

events.label: Morrison LNP
events.description: Scott Morrison becomes PM following Liberal leadership challenge against Turnbull. Wins 'miracle' 2019 election against Bill Shorten.

events.label: Robodebt ends
events.description: Government's automated welfare debt recovery scheme (Robodebt) begins unravelling. Later found to be unlawful. Royal Commission found it caused serious harm including suicides. $1.8bn in debts repaid.

events.label: Black Summer
events.description: Black Summer bushfires. 18.6 million hectares burned — larger than many countries. 33 direct deaths, 445 estimated smoke-related deaths. 3 billion animals killed or displaced.

events.label: Covid-19
events.description: COVID-19 pandemic. GDP fell 7% in June quarter 2020. JobKeeper wage subsidy cost $89bn. Borders closed for 2 years. RBA cut rates to 0.1%. $300bn in fiscal support deployed.

events.label: JobKeeper
events.description: JobKeeper wage subsidy introduced — $1,500 per fortnight per eligible employee. 3.8 million workers covered at peak. Total cost $89bn. Credited with preventing mass unemployment.

events.label: Ukraine war
events.description: Russia invades Ukraine. Global energy and food prices surge — LNG prices triple. Australian gas exporters benefit but domestic consumers face price spikes.

events.label: Albanese ALP
events.description: Anthony Albanese wins federal election. Labor returns after 9 years. Teal independents win six previously safe Liberal seats on climate and integrity platforms.

events.label: Rate hikes
events.description: RBA raises cash rate 13 times from 0.1% to 4.35% — the fastest tightening cycle in 30 years. Added ~$1,500/month to a typical $600k mortgage.

events.label: Voice referendum
events.description: Referendum on an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Voice to Parliament. Defeated 60.6% to 39.4%. First referendum defeat since 1977.

events.label: Housing Accord
events.description: National Housing Accord — agreement between federal, state and territory governments to build 1.2 million new homes by 2029. Target widely considered unlikely to be met given construction sector constraints.

events.label: Stage 3 tax cuts
events.description: Modified Stage 3 income tax cuts implemented — restructured by Albanese government to provide greater benefit to low and middle income earners than original legislated design.

events.label: Rate cuts
events.description: RBA begins cutting cash rate from 4.35% as inflation returns to target band. First cut in February 2025.

events.label: Albanese ALP (2nd term)
events.description: Anthony Albanese wins a historic second term in a Labor landslide — the biggest victory since 1943. Labor secures 94 seats. Peter Dutton loses his own seat of Dickson. Coalition reduced to 24 seats.
